title: 微软待办管理：怎样判断一个事项已准备好
topic: 微软待办管理：怎样判断一个事项已准备好

source.title: Backlog Management - Engineering Fundamentals Playbook
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 本课选取微软 Engineering Fundamentals Playbook 的完整 Backlog 页面。例句中的产品需求和团队约定是学习练习中的虚构情境，不代表 Microsoft 的统一优先级政策。页面原文有数处语法或措辞问题，批注明确指出并给出自然表达。
paragraphs: User stories have a clear acceptance criteria and definition of done.
Design activities are planned as part of the backlog (a design for a story that needs it should be done before it is added in a Sprint).
Consider the backlog refinement as an ongoing activity, that expands outside of the typical "Refinement meeting".
The team should decide on and have a clear understanding of a definition of ready and a definition of done.

The team should have a clear understanding of what constitutes good acceptance criteria for a story/task, and decide on how stories/tasks are handled. e.g., in some projects, stories are refined as a crew, but tasks are created by individual developers on an as-needed basis.

Technical debt is mostly due to shortcuts made in the implementation as well as the future maintenance cost as the natural result of continuous improvement. Shortcuts should generally be avoided. In some rare instances where they happen, prioritizing and planning improvement activities to reduce this debt at a later time is the recommended approach.
translations: 用户故事应有明确的验收标准和完成定义。原文写作 “a clear acceptance criteria”，冠词和复数名词不搭配；自然表达应为 “clear acceptance criteria” 或 “a clear acceptance criterion”。
设计活动应纳入待办事项；若某个故事需要设计，就应在该故事加入冲刺前完成设计。原文用 “added in a Sprint”，自然搭配是 “added to a sprint”。
待办事项细化应持续进行，不只发生在常规的“细化会议”中。原文在 activity 后多加了逗号，且 “expands outside” 不够自然；此处意在说细化工作会延伸到常规会议之外。
团队应共同确定并清楚理解“就绪定义”（Definition of Ready）和“完成定义”（Definition of Done）。这两项定义由团队协商，不是微软对所有项目设定的同一套标准。
团队应清楚什么样的用户故事或任务验收标准才算合格，并决定如何处理故事和任务。例如，有些项目由团队共同细化故事，而由开发人员在需要时创建具体任务。原文 “e.g.” 前的句号和大小写不规范。
技术债务多半来自实现时走的捷径，并可能带来未来维护成本。通常应避免走捷径；如果少数情况下确实采取了捷径，建议优先安排后续改进来降低技术债务。原句结构较难读，这里按其后两句给出的主张作保守转述。
fullTextParagraphs: User stories have a clear acceptance criteria and definition of done.
Design activities are planned as part of the backlog (a design for a story that needs it should be done before it is added in a Sprint).
Consider the backlog refinement as an ongoing activity, that expands outside of the typical "Refinement meeting".
The team should decide on and have a clear understanding of a definition of ready and a definition of done.

The team should have a clear understanding of what constitutes good acceptance criteria for a story/task, and decide on how stories/tasks are handled. e.g., in some projects, stories are refined as a crew, but tasks are created by individual developers on an as-needed basis.

Technical debt is mostly due to shortcuts made in the implementation as well as the future maintenance cost as the natural result of continuous improvement. Shortcuts should generally be avoided. In some rare instances where they happen, prioritizing and planning improvement activities to reduce this debt at a later time is the recommended approach.

notes.meaning: 明确的验收标准（原文有语法问题）
notes.explain: criteria 是复数，前面不能用 a。自然写法是 “clear acceptance criteria” 或 “a clear acceptance criterion”。练习使用前一种表达。
notes.example: Could we clarify the acceptance criteria before planning this story?

notes.phrase: before it is added in a Sprint
notes.explain: 这里 it 指需要设计的 story。英文习惯说 a story is added to a sprint，而不是 added in a sprint。
notes.example: The design should be complete before the story is added to a sprint.

notes.explain: refinement 不应只在一次固定会议中发生；新信息出现时，也可以继续更新待办事项。
notes.example: We can keep refining the backlog between meetings.

notes.phrase: a definition of ready and a definition of done
notes.explain: 这两项标准由团队共同约定：一个说明何时可以开始，一个说明何时算完成。
notes.example: Let’s agree on a definition of ready and a definition of done for this project.

notes.explain: crew 在这里指项目团队；来源只是举例说明有些项目共同细化故事、由开发人员按需创建任务，并未规定所有团队都必须这样做。
notes.example: We refined the story as a team and wrote the implementation tasks as needed.

notes.phrase: Technical debt is mostly due to shortcuts
notes.meaning: 技术债务多半源自实现时走捷径
notes.explain: 原句后半段结构不清；本课按紧接着的建议保守解释为捷径会带来未来维护负担，若确实发生就安排后续改进。
notes.example: The team planned work to reduce maintenance costs caused by an earlier shortcut.

scenario.title: A story is not ready for sprint planning
english: The team is reviewing a password-reset story before sprint planning. Its acceptance criteria say only “make the experience easier,” and the design is not finished.
One teammate wants to add the story to the sprint and decide the details later. You want the team to agree on what success means and finish the needed design first.
The team can then check the story against its shared definition of ready before planning it.
chinese: 团队在冲刺计划前检查一个密码重置故事。它的验收标准只写着“让体验更简单”，设计也还没完成。
一位同事想先把故事放进冲刺，细节之后再定。你希望团队先明确怎样才算成功，并完成所需设计。
之后团队可以根据共同约定的“就绪定义”检查这个故事，再安排计划。

firstAttempt.prompt: 一个资料导出功能的故事只有“让导出更方便”这条模糊标准，所需设计也没完成。请用英文建议先明确验收标准并完成设计，再检查是否达到团队的就绪定义。
firstAttempt.sample: Could we clarify the acceptance criteria and finish the design before we add this story to the sprint? Then we can check it against our definition of ready.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先明确怎么判断故事是否符合要求，并完成必需的设计；然后按团队约定的就绪定义检查。练习里的定义是团队示例，不代表 Microsoft 统一政策。

words.example: Could we clarify the acceptance criteria before planning this story?
words.translation: 我们能否在计划这个故事前明确验收标准？
words.note: 可测试的条件，帮助团队判断用户故事是否满足要求。原文的 “a clear acceptance criteria” 有单复数搭配问题。

words.collocation: do backlog refinement as an ongoing activity
words.example: We can refine the backlog as new information comes in.
words.translation: 有新信息时，我们可以继续细化待办事项。
words.note: 来源建议把它当作持续活动，不只局限在例行细化会议里。

words.meaning: 就绪定义；团队约定的开始条件
words.collocation: check a story against the definition of ready
words.example: Let’s check this story against our definition of ready.
words.translation: 我们按团队的就绪定义检查这个故事吧。
words.note: 由团队共同约定，说明哪些条件满足后可以开始处理，不是通用模板。

words.meaning: 完成定义；团队约定的完成条件
words.collocation: agree on a definition of done
words.example: The team agreed on a definition of done for this project.
words.translation: 团队为这个项目商定了完成定义。
words.note: 与就绪定义不同：它描述怎样才算完成。具体内容应由团队约定。

words.meaning: 用户故事；从用户需求角度写出的工作项
words.example: The team clarified the user story before estimating it.
words.translation: 团队在估算前明确了这个用户故事。
words.note: 本课语境里是待办列表中的需求项；不是完整的设计说明。

words.meaning: 技术债务；捷径带来的后续维护负担
words.collocation: plan improvements to reduce technical debt
words.example: The team planned an improvement to reduce technical debt from an earlier shortcut.
words.translation: 团队安排了一项改进，以降低之前走捷径带来的技术债务。
words.note: 来源说应尽量避免捷径；如果确有捷径，后续要优先安排改进。这里不把所有维护成本都直接等同于技术债。

structure.original: Design activities are planned as part of the backlog (a design for a story that needs it should be done before it is added in a Sprint).
analysis: 主句使用被动语态：Design activities 是主语，are planned 是谓语，表示设计活动被纳入待办计划。
括号补充一条时间要求：需要设计的故事要在加入 sprint 前完成设计。这里的 it 指 story。
原文 “added in a Sprint” 不够自然；说故事加入冲刺通常用 “added to a sprint”。
structure.transfer: Could we finish the design before we add this story to the sprint?

rewrite.bad: Let’s add the story to the sprint now and decide the acceptance criteria and design later.
rewrite.good: Could we clarify the acceptance criteria and finish the design before we add this story to the sprint? Then we can check it against our definition of ready.
rewrite.translation: 我们能否先明确验收标准并完成设计，再把故事加入冲刺？之后按团队的就绪定义检查。
rewrite.pattern: Could we [clarify the criteria] and [finish the required design] before we [add the story to the sprint]?

cloze.prompt: Could we clarify the acceptance ___ before planning this story?
cloze.why: acceptance criteria 是验收标准；该词在本课练习中按常见复数形式使用。

cloze.prompt: Finish the design before adding the story ___ the sprint.
cloze.why: 自然搭配是 add a story to a sprint。

cloze.prompt: Check the story against our definition of ___.
cloze.why: definition of ready 是团队约定的开始条件。

dictation.text: User stories need clear acceptance criteria and a definition of done.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 故事的验收条件
dictation.why: 听清验收标准和完成定义。这里采用自然改写，避免照读原文的冠词错误。

dictation.text: A design for a story that needs one should be finished before the story is added to a sprint.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 设计与进入冲刺的先后
dictation.why: 听出所需设计在故事进入 sprint 前完成。

apply.prompt: 团队习惯只在每周细化会议更新待办，但刚收到一条会改变需求的新信息。用英文建议怎样处理？
apply.sample: Could we keep refining the backlog as new information comes in, instead of waiting for the next refinement meeting?

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否在计划这个故事前明确验收标准？
translationPractice.answer: Could we clarify the acceptance criteria before planning this story?
translationPractice.why: 提出先补齐可判断的故事要求。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否先完成设计，再把这个故事加入冲刺？
translationPractice.answer: Could we finish the design before we add this story to the sprint?
translationPractice.why: 用 before 明确设计和加入 sprint 的先后。

translationPractice.prompt: 然后我们可以按团队的就绪定义检查它。
translationPractice.answer: Then we can check it against our definition of ready.
translationPractice.why: 说明按团队共同定义的条件检查故事是否 ready。

choice.prompt: 团队在周一的细化会议后收到新客户信息，可能改变一个故事的验收标准。来源建议如何处理待办细化？
options: Wait until the next formal refinement meeting and leave the story unchanged.
Move the story into the sprint immediately and update its criteria later.
Treat backlog refinement as ongoing and update the story as new information arrives.
choice.why: 原文建议待办细化持续进行，不限于例行的 refinement meeting；这不等于未经检查就把故事加入 sprint。

output.prompt: 团队成员对“什么时候可以开始一个故事”和“怎样才算完成”理解不一致。请用英文建议先共同约定 definition of ready 和 definition of done。
output.sample: Could we agree on a definition of ready and a definition of done for this project? That way, we’ll know what needs to be clear before work starts and what must be true before we call a story complete.
check: 是否提出共同约定 Definition of Ready？
是否提出共同约定 Definition of Done？
是否区分开始条件和完成条件？
